expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: "The union: `type Subscription = TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | ...`" and "The `switch` statement on `status`" — discriminant is the status field

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: "Four separate types (one per state): `TrialingSubscription` → has `trialEndDate` ... `CanceledSubscription` → has `cancelReason` enum and `voluntary: boolean`"

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: "Exhaustiveness checking: The `switch` statement on `status` will cause a TypeScript error if you add a new state but forget to handle it." — asserted as a property but no assertNever/never arm is shown; the code is not present ("Creating `src/subscription-types.ts` now...")

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Branded IDs are described only in the Insight box as a general rationale ("Without branding, TypeScript sees both `subscriptionId` and `customerId` as plain strings"); the actual design section lists no ID fields or branded types among the four variants

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: "The TODO at the bottom marks where state transition functions would go. You'll need to define which transitions are legal" — explicitly deferred to the user

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "A string-based status like `status: "canceled"` lets you accidentally access `renewal_date` on a canceled subscription. A discriminated union makes TypeScript prevent that at compile time."

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is "Four separate types (one per state)" joined in a union; no optional-field interface is proposed
